circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been home to Formula One's season finale since 2009. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One destination, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street-based track that winds around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds an FIA Grade 1 classification. It serves as the permanent home of the Formula One Australian Grand Prix, alongside hosting the Supercars Championship Melbourne SuperSprint and various support series throughout the year.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located near Spielberg in Styria, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods: first as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then following reconstruction and renaming as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003. The track underwent significant modifications between these eras, including a notable shortening of its original layout.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital city, situated adjacent to Baku Boulevard, with a lap distance of 6. 003 kilometers that ranks as the fourth-longest Formula One venue. The track first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onward, both organized by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit opened in 2004 as a 5. 412 km venue hosting various motorsport events, most notably the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which marked the first F1 race held in the Middle East. The track accommodated additional series including GP2 racing and Australian V8 Supercars (2006-2010), while also featuring 24-hour endurance competitions and multiple circuit configurations under its FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit is renowned as a versatile test of driver skill, featuring an eclectic mix of high-speed straights and technical corners. The venue accommodates over 140,000 spectators and maintains the highest FIA safety certification grade.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated near the town of Spa in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a fixture of international motorsport since 1925 and participated in Formula One's inaugural season in 1950. The venue has continuously hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361-kilometre Canadian racing venue hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond Formula One, the circuit has accommodated various international motorsport series, including World Sportscar Championship events, Champ Car competition, and multiple NASCAR categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility is primarily recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing events beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit has served as the venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural Formula One World Championship race in 1950. Following decades of alternating with other British circuits, the Grand Prix permanently returned to Silverstone from 1987 onwards, establishing it as the traditional home of motorsport's premier British event.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted Formula One's historic 1986 Hungarian Grand Prix, marking the sport's first championship race in Eastern Europe. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except for a 1980 closure during renovation, and earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its characteristic long straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track serves as a primary venue for Formula One and Japanese Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street-based racing layout positioned in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban environment. The track features several of the city's most recognizable entertainment venues and landmarks, such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a distinctive setting for motorsport competition.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City is a 4. 304 km circuit bearing the names of two brothers who both died in racing accidents: Ricardo in 1962 and Pedro in 1971. The track has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix in three distinct eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, with the event now officially designated as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging approximately 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the venue began hosting the Miami Grand Prix as part of the championship calendar starting in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street track that winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, circling the harbour district. Though officially recognized by both names, it is predominantly called "Monte Carlo" due to the majority of its layout occupying that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Situated in the Dutch dunes near the North Sea and approximately 35 kilometres west of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the Netherlands' return to Formula One in 2021 after a lengthy absence. The venue will continue staging the Dutch Grand Prix until 2026, when its partnership with the sport concludes.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aircraft accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and shares its facilities with a karting venue dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue in Saudi Arabia situated along the Red Sea waterfront, serving as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix starting from 2021. The track has also begun hosting an international electric racing championship event from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning regions in its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a diverse mix of straights and corners that test multiple aspects of driver and car performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 racing facility in Austin, Texas that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP's Americas round and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, along with various other series throughout its operating history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships during his tenure at Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seater racing, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance competition, including victories at Le Mans and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six Grand Prix victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, competing at the sport's highest level under his given name Gabriel Lourenzo Oliveira.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver secured runner-up finishes in consecutive championship seasons while driving for Mercedes, and has claimed ten race victories throughout his lengthy Formula One career. Bottas now represents Cadillac on the current grid.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan has appeared in seven Formula One races between 2024 and 2025 while maintaining a reserve role with Haas. Outside of his Grand Prix commitments, he competes in European Le Mans Series LMP2 competition for Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The AlphaTauri driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France internationally.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: A British driver competing for Ferrari, Hamilton shares the record for most championship titles with Schumacher at seven victories. He holds multiple performance records including the most race wins, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing considerable experience from his motorsport career. Beyond his Formula One involvement, he achieved a major milestone by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently races for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver competes for Ferrari in Formula One, where he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while driving for the Maranello-based squad.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again in 2022-2024. Currently, he competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship as a factory driver for BMW with WRT, while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Great Britain in Formula One, where he drives for McLaren and clinched the 2025 World Drivers' Championship with the team. The accomplished driver has secured 13 race victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Earlier in his career, he achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Checo Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from over 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while with Red Bull and has secured victories in six Grand Prix events throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver competing in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earned eight Grand Prix victories throughout his 14-year career in the sport. Known by his nickname "the Honey Badger", Ricciardo has since retired from Formula One racing.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car competition. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian racing driver competing in Formula One with Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese racing driver currently holding a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. He participated actively in Formula One competition spanning from 2021 through 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen competes for Red Bull Racing and has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024, along with 71 Grand Prix victories during his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently working as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport from 2022 to 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates from Enstone as Renault's factory Formula One team, having been rebranded under the Alpine sports car marque in 2021 after competing as Renault F1 Team. The outfit secured its only victory as Alpine when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained an intermittent presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with its current competitive entry operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished competitor, participating continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The team, colloquially referred to as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, has accumulated an unmatched record of success throughout its seven-decade presence in the sport.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American team owner Gene Haas founded this Formula One outfit in 2014, entering competition from the 2016 season onward. Leadership passed to Ayao Komatsu in early 2024 following the departure of the team's original principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise established in 1970, the outfit competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards as an independent constructor, achieving notable success in endurance motorsport including the 1989 Le Mans victory. After undergoing numerous transformations throughout its three-decade involvement in the sport, the organization departed Formula One in 2025 as one of the championship's longest-serving constructors before its acquisition by Audi in 2024.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, with full ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through both team ownership and engine supply. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team operates from Brackley under a German racing licence, with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff as of 2022. The marque's racing teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor based in Faenza that commenced operations in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second works team alongside Red Bull Racing. The outfit maintains a presence in Milton Keynes to facilitate coordination with its sister squad within the Red Bull Formula One programme.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as the second team operated by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with facilities in Milton Keynes, the team operates as part of Red Bull's dual-team structure in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing competes in Formula One under an Austrian licence while operating from England, representing one of two F1 teams within the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate. Established in 2005, the team was led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade history until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role thereafter.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerged following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has established itself as a significant force in the sport's history, competing under various title sponsorships including Atlassian in 2026.
